story.head: Kucherov’s favorite opponent
paras: The Blue Jackets (7-8-0) lost 5-2 to Buffalo on Friday, while the Lightning have won two in a row. The Lightning played last night, and the Blue Jackets are rested. Going in, the Lightning are third in the Atlantic (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets sixth in the Metropolitan (27th).
This season, the Blue Jackets have been outscored 47-38, but only 28-25 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 12-7.

The Lightning get into a lot of chippy games (4th) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (5th). They also keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), so the Blue Jackets may have a hard time getting pucks to the net against them. The Jackets get their defensemen shooting (4th), get a lot of their shots blocked (29th) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (28th). The Blue Jackets’ struggling power play gets a tough test from the Lightning’s penalty killers.

Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in seven straight games against Columbus. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Zach Werenski (2 G / 12 A / 14 P in 15 GP) is next in line.

Dennis Hildeby (2-0-1 / .885 SV% in 3 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay. Columbus has two options in net: Jet Greaves (2-6-0 / .879 SV% in 8 GS) and Cam Talbot (5-2-0 / .909 SV% in 7 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Greaves got the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Rick Bowness likes to send Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Guentzel, Point and Kucherov.
